title: Home lab network experiment
summary: Build a low-cost home lab to test routing, DNS, and monitoring.
details:
Scope
- Switch and two used mini PCs
- OpenWrt router image
- Uptime Kuma monitoring

Goals
- Stable intranet
- Packet capture baseline
- Documentation for future nodes
spark: I finally found spare hardware that is good enough for a weekend proof of concept.
next: Order the used mini PC and schedule the cabling weekend.
blockers: Waiting for one network switch to arrive. Need a clear test plan before touching production WiFi.

notes.text: Bought a second-hand switch. Need to test VLANs before adding media server.
Drafted a simple test checklist: DNS, latency, ARP, packet loss.

title: Balcony vegetable garden v2
summary: Improve a small balcony garden with better containers, drip irrigation, and shade control.
details:
Current setup
- Two 15L fabric pots
- Cherry tomatoes
- Basil and chives

Changes this season
- Add a trellis for tomatoes
- Install a battery drip line
- Test a raised edge for lettuce

Observations
- East sun is strong between 08:00 and 11:00
- Wind can dry soil fast on exposed days
spark: Last year the basil bolted after one heat wave, so I want a more forgiving setup.
next: Measure the balcony rail spacing and order the trellis.
blockers: Need to check building rules about hanging water from the second floor.

notes.text: Noticed aphids near the basil. Try water spray first before buying anything.
The old drip line works but needs a slower emitter for pots.

title: Personal finance dashboard
summary: Create a simple local dashboard for budgets, savings goals, and recurring subscriptions.
details:
Version 3 focus
- Import CSV from two banks
- Keep data local in SQLite
- Show monthly burn rate

Non-goals
- No credit scoring
- No automatic trading
- No cloud sync for now

Risks
- CSV formats change often
- Some subscriptions are hard to classify automatically
spark: I keep forgetting small subscriptions, and a local-only tool feels more trustworthy than another SaaS login.
next: Write a parser for the second bank CSV and add a manual override table.
blockers: One bank exports only the last 90 days, which limits trend charts.

notes.text: Decided to store raw CSV in a read-only folder and processed data in SQLite.
Found duplicate subscription entries. Need dedupe by merchant and amount.

title: Weekend sourdough schedule
summary: Build a repeatable weekend sourdough routine using a small starter and an oven-safe pot.
details:
Idea
- Keep starter at 20% hydration
- Feed once per day on weekdays
- Bake one loaf on Saturday

Open questions
- What flour mix gives better crust?
- Should I use a 24h cold proof or a 12h room proof?
- What is the minimum oven temperature my oven really holds?

Notes from experiments
- Day one loaf was dense
- Day two loaf tore open before it browned
spark: Baking bread feels calming, and I have more spare time during the week now.
next: Measure a 7-day hydration test with the same flour and scale.
blockers: The oven temperature is inconsistent, so crust color is hard to predict.

notes.text: Starter smelled pleasant but was slower to rise than expected.
Try a longer bulk fermentation at 24C next weekend.

title: Local history podcast
summary: Record short interviews and walking segments about local places, people, and old maps.
details:
Concept
- One place per episode
- 15 to 20 minutes total
- Mix of interview, narration, and sound

Possible episodes
- The old tram line through the park
- The café that became a library
- The river cleanup after the flood

Production needs
- Lavalier microphone
- Simple noise gate
- Map overlay template
spark: Neighbours often mention stories I have never heard, and they might disappear if not recorded.
next: Interview one neighbor about the old tram line and record a 5 minute pilot.
blockers: Street noise is high during work hours, so outdoor takes are limited.

notes.text: Found a map photo from 1932. Need higher resolution before using it.
A neighbour agreed to talk on Friday after 16:00.

title: Retro handheld repair log
summary: Document the repair of an old handheld device, including screen replacement, cleaning, and battery upgrade.
details:
Target device
- Model with cracked glass
- Dead battery
- Stuck shoulder buttons

Repair steps
- Open shell with plastic picks
- Replace battery
- Clean contacts
- Install new screen glass
- Test all buttons and charging

Parts needed
- Screen assembly
- Battery
- Shoulder button pads
- Thermal pad for charging port
spark: This device has a good screen before the crack, and the parts are cheap enough to be worth doing carefully.
next: Order replacement screen, battery, and shoulder button pads.
blockers: Need a precision screwdriver set for the small Phillips screws.

notes.text: Battery bulges slightly. Do not press the shell while opening.
Found the shoulder button pads are worn on the right side.

title: Remote work cabin retreat
summary: Plan a short-term cabin rental for focused work blocks, with offline fallback and local meeting spots.
details:
Dream setup
- 3 to 5 night stays
- One room with a good chair
- Fast local internet
- Quiet walking path

Checklist
- Confirm power backup
- Test video call stability
- Find nearby café with outlets
- Pack laptop, charger, and paper notebook

Parking reasons
- Current job schedule is too tight
- Cost needs a clear monthly cap
- Better to test with one weekend first
spark: Remote work works well, but my home desk gets interrupted too often during the day.
next: Revisit in spring when the schedule is calmer and permits are clearer.
blockers: Cost is still too uncertain and the desired cabin is often booked by local residents.

notes.text: One cabin had fast internet but no reliable backup power.
Maybe use a cheaper guesthouse and work from a nearby library.

title: Open source CLI theme pack
summary: Create a small theme pack for terminal apps with accessible contrast and simple configuration.
details:
Current scope
- 4 color themes
- One config file
- Install via git or npm
- README with screenshots

Parked because
- Maintainer time is limited
- Need feedback from actual users
- Existing theme frameworks may already solve most of it

Possible restart trigger
- Five users request the same theme
- A conference talk gives a deadline
- The upstream project adopts a stable theming API
spark: I keep copying colors between tools and losing contrast, so a shared theme would save time.
next: Collect feedback from five users before rewriting the config loader.
blockers: Time conflicts with the main job and there is no clear distribution path yet.

notes.text: The blue theme passes contrast for text but fails for inactive borders.
Maybe publish one theme as a proof before building the full pack.
